hook_text: Three crosses on squared paper and a ruler through zero. The slope is your resistor.
clip_script: Volts up the side, amps along the bottom, labelled with units, even scales from zero. Plot the three means as neat crosses. Ruler through the origin, tilt until it is close to all three. One straight line, never a zigzag. A straight line through zero means proportional: double the volts, double the amps. That is Ohm's law on paper. Now the gradient: two far-apart points, volts difference over amps difference. 4.4 over 0.044 is 100. Volts per amp is ohms, and the bands said 100. Conclusion in three sentences: straight line so proportional, about 100 ohms matching the bands, cells lost a little inside.
visual_style: Whiteboard graph with axes labelled; three crosses appearing; a ruler swinging to fit through the origin; a rise and run triangle drawn on the line with 4.4 and 0.044; the number 100.
mood: Steady and clarifying, like watching a result appear.
pacing: Axes, crosses, ruler, straight line, meaning, gradient, match, conclusion.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and plot your own three readings tonight.
